title: Ledger held-out retrieval evaluation case (v1)
description: One machine-checkable query/expected-answer case for the Ledger document-retrieval evaluation corpus described in docs/subsystems/LEDGER-MARKDOWN-INDEXING-AND-DOCUMENT-NAVIGATION-CANON.md section 12. Cases are stored as JSON Lines, one object per line, split across train.jsonl / dev.jsonl / heldout.jsonl. This schema describes exactly one line of any of those files.

id.description: Stable, corpus-unique case identifier. Never renumbered after first publication; a retired case is marked instead of having its id reused.

split.description: authoring/train split | development/tuning split | held-out test split, per canon section 12.1. Tokenizer, BM25 weights, query normalization, title-chain treatment, expansion parameters, and rank tuning may use train/dev only. heldout is run exactly once per frozen candidate and is never used to tune.

case_type.description: Primary coverage category this case exercises, drawn from canon section 12.3's minimum query classes plus the task's identifier/short-query/CJK/stale-revision requirements.

tags.description: Secondary/free-form coverage labels. A case may legitimately serve more than one coverage class (e.g. an environment-variable list item is both list_item and identifier); case_type names the primary class used for per-category reporting, tags record the rest.

source_corpus.description: Which of the two required real corpora (canon 12.3: 'real Membrane documentation' plus 'a second real corpus with different authoring style/structure') this case's target document(s) belong to. research-papers = docs/research/papers/** (dense academic PDF-extracted prose, citation-heavy, largely undocumented GFM structure) as the second, structurally different real corpus.

query.description: The literal query text a retrieval harness should issue. For non_ascii_cjk/mixed_script cases this is non-ASCII (or mixed-script) text verbatim, never a transliteration.

query_script.description: Script/language hint for non-Latin or mixed-script queries (e.g. 'ja', 'zh', 'ko', 'mixed-en-ja'). null for plain-ASCII queries.

status.description: match: at least one target below is a correct retrieval outcome. no_match: no document in this corpus correctly answers the query (negative case; correct system behavior is abstention, not a best-effort guess). relocation: the naive/literal target is stale, retired, or not-yet-landed; the listed target(s) are the CURRENT correct answer, and notes explains the relocation/refusal semantics being tested (canon section 7.4 stale/typed-relocation contract).

match_mode.description: single/any_of: retrieval succeeds if it surfaces at least one listed target (any_of is used when more than one target is independently acceptable, e.g. a naming-drift case with both the old and new document). all_of: a correct answer must synthesize evidence from every listed target (multi_section_synthesis cases).

document.description: Repository-root-relative path to the expected source document. Every path here also appears in manifest.json with its sha256 at authoring time.

heading.description: Exact heading text (without the leading '#' markers) of the expected section, verbatim as it appears in the source document. null when the case targets document-level content that precedes any heading (e.g. YAML frontmatter, page chrome in a scraped article) or when the document has no GFM heading structure at all. This is a human-readable alias for locating the section, not canonical node identity -- consistent with the Ledger canon's section 7.3 treatment of heading slugs.

quote.description: An exact, verbatim, single-line-safe substring of the source document that a correct retrieval/resolution must be able to reproduce or point at. Used both as machine-checkable ground truth (grep-verified at corpus-build time; see build_corpus.py in the corpus provenance) and as a human-readable pointer. null only when a case is document-level (case_type=exact_document) and no specific span is being tested.

plausible_distractors.description: Repository-root-relative paths a naive lexical/BM25 matcher might over-rank for this query despite not answering it. Populated mainly on negative_no_answer and stale_relocation cases to make false-positive scoring possible; empty array otherwise.

notes.description: Free-text rationale: why this case exists, what specific failure mode it is designed to catch, and any authoring caveats (e.g. 'this document has no GFM headings'). Never omitted -- use an empty string only if truly nothing needs saying.
